name: Anise hyssop

schedule.notes: Surface-sow; light required. Needs cold stratification — refrigerate seeds 2 to 3 weeks first.
Leaves anytime; flower spikes when half-open for the strongest scent.

harvest.cues: Leaves bright green and anise-scented. Flower spikes lavender-purple, half-open.
harvest.storageNotes: Dries beautifully. Petals are edible; sprinkle on salads or steep for tea.

varieties.name: Blue Fortune
varieties.notes: Long bloom season, doesn't self-seed. Pollinator favorite.

varieties.name: Korean Mint
varieties.notes: Slightly minty-anise. Used in Korean cuisine.

notes: Bees go wild for it. Native to North American prairies — drought-tolerant once established. Self-seeds prolifically unless you cut flower stalks before seeds set.
